?Court No. - 74
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 17353 of 2023
Applicant :- Sudhir Kumar @ Bauwa

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Munna Pandey,Harsha Pandey,Harshit Pandey Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
Heard Sri Harshit Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ravi Kant Kushwaha, learned AGA for the State.

The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
265 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Sumerpur,
District Hamirpur during pendency of the trial.

FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and his family members and according to the FIR marriage of the applicant was performed with the daughter of the informant in the year 2019 and applicant and his family members tortured the daughter of the informant for want of dowry and on 27.06.2022 applicant and his family members committed murder of the daughter of the informant.

Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that entire allegation made against the applicant is totally false and baseless and applicant neither tortured the deceased nor demanded any dowry and being husband, applicant has been falsely implicated by the informant in the present matter.

He further submits that his wife committed suicide and this fact is itself evident from the post mortem Sudhir Kumar @ Bauwa vs State Of U.P. on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191795286/
1 report.

sentences.text: He next submits that marriage of the deceased was performed with the applicant against her wishes as she was having some love affair with somebody else and only due to this reason she committed suicide after her marriage within two years.

He further submits that informant and three other family members of the deceased were examined by the trial court as PW-1, PW-2, PW-3 and PW-4 and all have turned hostile and they did not support the prosecution case and categorically stated before the trial court that applicant never demanded any dowry and deceased committed suicide.
He next submits that the certified copies of their statements have been annexed as Annexures 10 and 11 to the affidavit filed in support of present bail application.
He further submits that applicant in the present matter is in jail since 03.07.2022.

Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is the husband of the deceased but could not dispute the fact that when informant and his family members appeared before the trial court then they did not support the version of the FIR and they have turned hostile.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

Although, applicant is the husband of the deceased and his wife died within two years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances and in the FIR there was also allegation of demand of dowry but it appears that during the course of trial informant and other three prosecution witnesses have turned hostile.

The certified copies of their statements have been annexed as Annexures 10 and 11 to the affidavit and from its perusal it appears that informant appeared before the trial court as PW-1 and stated that she under some confusion lodged FIR of the present case and applicant and his family members never demanded any dowry and they did not ever torture the deceased,
therefore, considering the fact that material witnesses of the fact including informant have turned hostile during trial and applicant in the present matter is in jail since 03.07.2022, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant - Sudhir Kumar @ Bauwa be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
